passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: The following discussion and analysis should be read in conjunction with Part I, Item 1, Business, our audited Consolidated Financial Statements and the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements in this Annual Report. RECENT DEVELOPMENTS Please refer to the “Financial Results and Operating Information” and “Liquidity and Capital Resources” sections of Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations in this Annual Report for additional information. Acquisitions Delaware Basin JV Acquisition - On May 28, 2025, we completed the Delaware Basin JV Acquisition for $941 million. Pursuant to the purchase agreement, we paid $550 million in cash, including post-closing adjustments, which we funded with short-term borrowings and issued approximately 4.9 million shares of ONEOK common stock to the seller with a fair value of $391 million as of the closing date. Following the completion of the transaction, it is now a wholly owned subsidiary. EnLink Acquisition - On January 31, 2025, we completed the EnLink Acquisition. Pursuant to the EnLink Merger Agreement, each publicly held common unit of EnLink was exchanged for a fixed ratio of 0.1412 shares of ONEOK common stock, including EnLink Units that were exchanged for all previously outstanding Series B Preferred Units immediately prior to closing. We issued 41 million shares of common stock with a fair value of $4.0 billion as of the closing date of the EnLink Acquisition. EnLink is now a wholly owned subsidiary. For additional information on our most recent acquisitions, see Part II, Item 8, Note B of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements in this Annual Report. See Part I, Item 1A “Risk Factors” for further discussion of risks related to these transactions. Joint Ventures Eiger Express Pipeline - In 2025, we, WhiteWater, MPLX LP and Enbridge Inc., through the existing Matterhorn joint venture, announced the new approximately 450-mile, 48-inch Eiger Express Pipeline, designed to transport up to approximately 3.7 Bcf/d of natural gas from the Permian Basin to Katy, Texas. WhiteWater will construct and operate the pipeline. Our total ownership interest in the pipeline will be 25.5%, which includes a 15% interest held directly in the Eiger joint venture with the remainder held through Matterhorn. We expect to invest a total of approximately $350 million into this project, which is expected to be completed in mid-2028. BridgeTex Additional Interest Acquisition - On July 22, 2025, we completed the BridgeTex Additional Interest Acquisition. Pursuant to the purchase agreement, we paid approximately $270 million in cash, which we funded with short-term borrowings. Following the completion of the transaction, we now have a 60% ownership interest in BridgeTex. Texas City Logistics and MBTC Pipeline - In February 2025, we announced definitive agreements to form joint ventures with MPLX LP to construct a 400 MBbl/d liquified petroleum gas export terminal in Texas City, Texas, and a new 24-inch pipeline from our Mont Belvieu, Texas, storage facility to the new terminal. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: You should consider carefully the following discussion of risks, as well as all of the other information contained in this Annual Report. Our business, financial conditions, results of operations or prospects could be materially and adversely affected by any of these risks or uncertainties. RISK FACTORS RELATED TO OUR BUSINESS AND INDUSTRY If the level of drilling in the regions in which we operate declines substantially near our assets, our volumes and revenues could decline. Our gathering and transportation pipeline systems are dependent upon production from natural gas and crude oil wells, which naturally decline over time. As a result, our cash flows associated with these wells may also decline over time. In order to maintain or increase throughput levels on our gathering and transportation pipeline systems and the asset utilization rates at our processing and fractionation facilities, we must continually obtain new supplies. Our ability to maintain or expand our businesses depends largely on the level of drilling and production by third parties in the regions in which we operate. Our natural gas, NGL and crude supply volumes may be impacted if producers curtail or redirect drilling and production activities. Drilling and production are impacted by factors beyond our control, including: • demand and prices for natural gas, NGLs, Refined Products and crude oil; • producers’ access to capital; • producers’ finding and development costs of reserves; • producers’ ability to secure drilling and completion crews and equipment; • producers’ desire and ability to obtain necessary permits, drilling rights and surface access in a timely manner and on reasonable terms; • crude oil and associated natural gas field characteristics and production performance; • regulatory compliance and environmental or other governmental regulations; • reserve performance; and • capacity constraints and/or shutdowns on the pipelines that transport crude oil, natural gas, NGLs and Refined Products from producing areas and our facilities. Commodity prices are subject to significant volatility. Drilling and production activity levels may vary across our geographic areas; however, a prolonged period of low commodity prices may reduce drilling and production activities across all areas. If we are not able to obtain new supplies to replace the natural decline in volumes from existing production or reductions in volumes because of competition, throughput on our gathering and transportation pipeline systems and the utilization rates of our processing and fractionation facilities would decline, which could adversely affect our business, results of operations, financial position and cash flows. Our operating results may be adversely affected by unfavorable economic and market conditions. Uncertainty or adverse changes in economic conditions worldwide, in the United States, or in the economic regions in which we operate, could negatively affect the crude oil and natural gas markets, resulting in reduced demand and increased price competition for our services and products, or otherwise adversely affect our business, results of operations, financial position and cash flows. credit_strengths.text: ONEOK's operating cash flow covers capital spending and dividends, with free cash flow remaining positive after growth investment. The fee-based midstream model supports cash generation even as commodity prices fluctuate, and operating income has grown steadily across the disclosed annual trend, providing a solid base for debt service.

Interest coverage sits comfortably above the sector median, reflecting the earnings power of the expanded asset base following recent acquisitions. Operating income covers interest expense by a healthy multiple, and the current ratio, while below one, is consistent with the sector's working capital profile for midstream operators.

key_risks.text: The risk factors highlight that gathering and transportation systems depend on production from wells that naturally decline, and that a prolonged period of low commodity prices could reduce drilling and production across all areas. If new supplies are not obtained to replace declining volumes, throughput and revenues could fall, pressuring cash flows and leverage.

Leverage remains elevated following the EnLink and Delaware Basin acquisitions, with gross leverage above four times and net leverage near the sector median. The indicative financial risk profile is aggressive, and a modest EBITDA decline or debt increase would push leverage toward the next threshold, limiting financial flexibility.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Free cash flow to debt is modest, and the company relies on operating cash flow to service a large debt stack. With cash balances minimal, debt service depends on continued cash generation. The current portion of long-term debt and short-term borrowings require refinancing or repayment, and the maturity profile is not detailed in the provided data.

Interest coverage provides a cushion, but the absolute interest burden is significant. Capitalized interest is excluded from interest expense, and the debt sum may not capture all obligations. The company's ability to refinance maturing debt at reasonable rates is critical, especially given the aggressive financial risk profile and limited headroom to the next leverage threshold.

overall_credit_view.text: ONEOK's credit profile reflects a large, fee-based midstream asset base with stable cash flows, but leverage is elevated following recent acquisitions. The indicative financial risk profile is aggressive, and the company has limited headroom before breaching the next leverage threshold. Shareholder distributions absorb a substantial portion of free cash flow, constraining deleveraging.

The credit outlook is stable but sensitive to commodity price declines and production volumes. The company's scale and integrated network provide some resilience, but the aggressive financial risk profile and high leverage relative to cash flow warrant monitoring. Future deleveraging depends on EBITDA growth and disciplined capital allocation.

credit_strengths.text: ONEOK 的營運現金流足以覆蓋資本開支及股息，在增長投資後自由現金流仍保持正數。以費用為基礎的中游模式支持現金產生，即使商品價格波動亦然，而經營收入在已披露的年度趨勢中穩步增長，為償債提供穩固基礎。
利息覆蓋率穩居行業中位數以上，反映近期收購後擴大資產基礎的盈利能力。經營收入以穩健倍數覆蓋利息開支，而流動比率雖低於一，但與中游營運商所屬行業的營運資金狀況一致。

key_risks.text: 風險因素強調，集輸及運輸系統依賴自然遞減的油井產量，而商品價格長期低迷可能減少所有地區的鑽探及生產。若未能獲得新供應以替代遞減產量，輸送量及收入可能下降，對現金流及槓桿構成壓力。
在收購 EnLink 及 Delaware Basin 後，槓桿仍然偏高，總槓桿高於四倍，淨槓桿接近行業中位數。指示性財務風險狀況為進取，而 EBITDA 輕微下降或債務增加將推動槓桿逼近下一門檻，限制財務靈活性。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 自由現金流對債務比率適中，公司依賴營運現金流償付龐大債務。現金結餘極少，償債取決於持續現金產生。長期債務的流動部分及短期借款需要再融資或償還，而所提供數據並無詳細到期結構。
利息覆蓋提供緩衝，但絕對利息負擔重大。資本化利息不計入利息開支，而債務總額可能未涵蓋所有義務。公司能否以合理利率為到期債務再融資至關重要，尤其考慮到進取的財務風險狀況及距離下一槓桿門檻的有限空間。

overall_credit_view.text: ONEOK 的信用狀況反映龐大、以費用為基礎的中游資產基礎及穩定現金流，但近期收購後槓桿偏高。指示性財務風險狀況為進取，而公司在觸及下一槓桿門檻前空間有限。股東分派吸納自由現金流的重大部分，限制去槓桿。
信用展望穩定，但對商品價格下跌及產量敏感。公司的規模及綜合網絡提供一定韌性，但進取的財務風險狀況及相對於現金流的高槓桿值得監察。未來去槓桿取決於 EBITDA 增長及嚴謹的資本配置。
